evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said 'This should take about five to ten minutes of your time. And then we'll be able to build you an accurate quote that you can depend on. Sounds good.' Customer responded 'Okay. That'll work.' — framing present but rushed past without a real wait for confirmation, no explicit yes before moving to agenda.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked 'Do you have any concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' — but only AFTER already asking for moving day and beginning logistics probing with 'Can you have like a specific day that you're looking for?' The question came out of order.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer stated 'No, I'm just trying to get a, get a price more than anything. It's a pretty straightforward move.' — no concern was raised, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns were raised by the customer, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep gathered: property type (storage rooms + house), floor/stories (garage/first floor), number of rooms (three storage areas), walking distance (checked for access concerns), additional rooms (garage details), special considerations (glass jewelry cat needing wrapping, metal/wicker cabinet, bicycles, loose items), dimensions (10x15, 8x10, 5x8 units). All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' — only discussed how many boxes the customer had.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asked 'Do you happen to know how many boxes are we moving?' and customer replied 'probably thirty boxes.' Box count was addressed.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave typical range: 'a typical ten by fifteen storage unit would normally takes two movers that is between four and a half to six and a half hours' and personalized: 'in your case... we'll send out four movers and two trucks. Estimated time is 55 and a half hours. The estimated cost in case they end up five and a half hours would be $2,392.' Both anchor and personalization present.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed: hourly rate ($96/hour), trip fee ($2,140), what's included (truck, gas, insurance, tools, pads, wraps). Also framed: 'time-based pricing' and 'you only need to pay once the job is done and only for the actual hours' — the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute-increments language not explicitly stated, but time-based commitment framing present. Fee transparency and commitment framing both covered.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: After the estimate, customer said 'Alright, yeah, that's gonna be a bit high, I'll probably end up doing, doing most of it myself.' Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or any confirmation check. The rep moved directly to cost-reduction options ('Let me check if we just move it for three movers') without the pause/confirmation frame.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'Finally we have on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' Discount terms (discounting immediately if late) are clearly stated.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'So first is that we have no worry damage coverage included on the early rate that you're paying us. We will provide up to $2,000 per move. That is to repair replace and reimburse for your items.' The $2,000 and repair/replace/reimburse language are present. Built-in framing: 'included on the early rate' (not an add-on). However, the 'no deductible / no fine print' framing was not explicitly stated; rep said 'included' but did not explicitly call out 'no deductible' or 'no fine print.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: After the Two Promises section, the rep said 'And the best part is that there's no hidden fees of any type...' and then pivoted directly to logistics and pricing discussion. The rep never asked 'Does that put those to rest?' or a closing-the-loop version. Additionally, this covers ground (no hidden fees) that wasn't directly about the Two Promises themselves, so it reads as a continuation, not a close.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: After pricing discussion and customer hesitation ('that's gonna be a bit high'), the rep offered alternatives but never asked a genuine version of 'What's still concerning you about this move?' The call moved to cost reduction without a real final concerns probe.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' — the call moved directly from cost-reduction discussion to the close.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked a clear 'Would you like our help with your move?' The call ended with: 'Sure, I can send you a, a, an email. So just in case if you wanted to move forward, then just feel free to email us back, call us or text us anyway...' This is an offer to send materials, not an explicit ask for the business. No ask at all on this call.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep stated: 'there's no deposit required. No, I, and securing your spot you can always give us a call at anytime.' Rate lock is not explicitly mentioned; this language is about no deposit and flexibility to call back, not a rate-lock guarantee.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: No booking was confirmed. Customer said 'let me think about it a little bit' and 'Do you have a quote number or anything you can get?' Rep responded with 'Sure, I can send you a, a, an email... just feel free to email us back, call us or text us anyway, there's no deposit required.' The call ended with the quote being sent; no date, phone number, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or crew notes were confirmed.

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive logistics details across three separate locations (storage units and final destination) with precise dimensions, access information, and special-handling items, creating a solid foundation for an accurate estimate.
coaching_note: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' — the call ended with an offer to email the quote instead of a direct ask for the business, leaving the sale entirely to follow-up rather than securing it on the call itself.
